newsitem.title: UK: UK sleepwalking into federal Europe - Goldsmith.
newsitem.headline: UK sleepwalking into federal Europe - Goldsmith.

text.p: The leader of Britain's Referendum Party said on Saturday the British people were sleepwalking into surrendering the nation to a federal Europe.

Billionaire Sir James Goldsmith told the inaugural conference of the party whose sole aim is to secure a referendum on European integration that British sovereignty was threatened by "the backroom dealings of politicians".
"Now the trap is being closed. We...are being led blindfold into a federal superstate," he told some 4,000 supporters.
Goldmsith, who has pledged to spend some 20 million pounds ($31 million) on an election campaign, rejected suggestions that his party was made up of "little Englanders,"

"The Little Englanders are those who would transform this ancient nation into a mere province of the European Union," he told an audience of celebrities, disaffected Conservatives and several members of the European parliament.
The larger than expected turnout at the conference belied attempts by established parties to dismiss the impact of the Referendum Party, founded by Goldsmith less than a year ago.
Prime Minister John Major, whose Conservatives are more than 20 points behind opposition Labour in opinion polls, has dismissed the Referendum Party as a "fringe organisation."
But political analysts say that even a small number of votes for the Referendum Party could lead to defeat for some Conservative candidates in closely-fought seats.
Goldsmith claims increasing support from traditional Conservative voters fearful of European federalism and the influence of Brussels in British life.

He declined to spell out precisely what question the proposed referendum would put to the British people but made clear that the issue goes far beyond whether Britain should join a single European currency.
He said his own preference was for "a new Europe -- a Europe that draws its strengths from its extraordinary diversity. A Europe that is built on its true pillars -- its ancient nations".
The Referendum Party plans to field about 600 candidates in general elections which must be held by May 1997. Goldsmith has said it does not seek power and will disband once it has achieved its goal.
Celebrities including actor Edward Fox and millionaire zoo onwer John Aspinall recalled wars fought by Britain to repel foreign invaders.
"In this century a million Englishmen have given up their lives so that we should remain free, free from a German-dominated Europe," Aspinall told the conference.
"We offer our friendship to the European nations, including Germany, on a platter -- but not our freedom. That is not negotiable," he added.
